title: Hook: The Disappearing Light
text: Have you ever wondered why the sky is bright and yellow sometimes, but dark and black at other times? And where does the bright light go when you sleep?

title: Socratic Thinking: Look Up!
text: If you look up at the sky during the day, what is the brightest thing you see? Why do you think it feels so warm when you stand outside?

content.title: The Sun in the Day Sky
content.description: A bright yellow circle representing the Sun with a few fluffy clouds.

title: Reveal: The Mighty Sun
text: It is the Sun! The Sun is a huge, glowing ball of fire. It gives us heat and bright light during the day. Without the Sun, the Earth would be very cold and dark.

content.definition: The star around which the earth orbits, providing light and heat.

content.question: What gives us heat and light during the day?

title: Reflection: What if?
text: Imagine if the Sun never came up in the morning. What would happen to all the plants, trees, and animals?

content.title: Don't Look Directly!
content.text: Never look directly at the Sun! It is so bright that it can hurt your eyes.

title: Connection: The Big Bulb
text: Just like a giant light bulb lights up your entire room, the Sun is nature's giant light bulb that lights up the whole Earth!

content.title: Mastery: Feel the Warmth
content.text: Go outside with an adult during a sunny day. Stand in the sunlight for a minute, then stand in the shade. Do you feel the difference in warmth?

title: Hook: The Magic of the Night
text: But what happens when the Sun goes to sleep? The sky turns dark, and tiny twinkling lights magically appear. Who turns them on?

title: Socratic Thinking: Counting the Twinkles
text: Have you ever tried counting the twinkling lights at night? And have you noticed the big, white glowing object? Why do you think it changes its shape?

content.title: The Night Sky
content.description: A crescent moon with twinkling stars.

title: Reveal: The Moon and Stars
text: At night, we see the Moon and the Stars. The Moon does not have its own light; it shines because the Sun's light bounces off it! Stars are actually huge glowing balls of fire, but they look tiny because they are very, very far away.

content.definition: The large round object that circles the Earth and shines at night by reflecting light from the sun.
A huge glowing ball of gas in the sky that twinkles at night.

content.question: Why do stars look so tiny?
options: Because they are very far away
Because they are afraid of us

content.title: Teacher Tip: Moon Shapes
content.text: Tell students that the moon doesn't actually change shape; the sun just lights up different parts of it!

title: Reflection: Moon Drawings
text: Draw a picture of the Moon you saw last night. Was it perfectly round like a ball, or shaped like a banana?

title: Connection: Changing Dough
text: The Moon appears to change its shape in the sky, just like a piece of clay or dough can be rolled into different shapes like a circle or a crescent.

content.title: Mastery: Night Sky Explorer
content.text: Look at the night sky tonight with your parents. Try to find the Moon. What shape is it today? See if you can spot the brightest star!
